tools.name: enrich_catalog
tools.description: For retailers and marketplaces (API key required): up to 50 products per call (SKU with title, URL or GTIN) in; each product's compatibility attributes out (standards it takes and provides, numeric limits, evidence level, freshness), ready to add to a product feed or UCP catalog so agents can match

tools.name: verify_page
tools.description: Call this before you tell someone a web page, site or deploy is done or working, or before relying on another agent's "it's live": we open the public page in a separate browser (desktop or mobile) and check what you list. It loads; this text is visible; this link or button leads to this address; no

tools.name: verify_mcp
tools.description: Call this before you recommend, install or rely on an MCP server, after deploying one, or when a connector seems broken: we connect as an MCP client, list its tools, check each has a usable input schema and description, confirm the tools you name exist, and optionally run one sample call on a read-o

tools.name: launch_check
tools.description: Call this after building or deploying an MCP server or paid agent API, or when its listings may be out of date: we check it works (as verify_mcp does), then look it up in the official MCP Registry (and whether the listed version is current), Glama, PulseMCP, the x402 Bazaar, npm and PyPI, plus its s

tools.name: publish_to_registry
tools.description: Call this to get an MCP server into the official MCP Registry (which Glama, PulseMCP and others import from) without mcp-publisher or DNS: first call with url returns a one-line file to host at https://<domain>/.well-known/mcp-registry-auth; once it's up, call again with publisher_id and we publish

tools.name: check_payment_setup
tools.description: Call this after building or changing a paid (x402) endpoint, or when agents' payments fail: we call it unpaid like a paying agent, read the 402, and check the payment request parses (v1 or v2), the token's EIP-712 domain (extra.name/version) matches the contract on-chain (the usual cause of 'invalid

tools.name: watch_listing
tools.description: Call this after launching an MCP server or paid agent API to keep it findable: we run launch_check today and every day for 30 days, and tell your webhook (signed) when something changes: the server stops answering, the registry listing falls behind a release, a directory drops it, robots.txt starts

tools.name: reliability_score
tools.description: Before paying an unfamiliar x402 API, look up its payment-readiness score (0-100) from our daily unpaid checks of the x402 Bazaar: how many of its endpoints would accept an agent's payment, and the common problems. Free.

tools.name: launch_plan
tools.description: For sellers: 30 days of official MCP Registry publishing on every new version, a daily listing watch (registry, Glama, x402 Bazaar, npm, PyPI, health) and daily payment checks of up to 10 x402 endpoints, with one signed webhook. $12 per 30 days; renew with plan_id.

tools.name: launch_plan_status
tools.description: Where a Launch Plan stands: listings, registry version and each paid endpoint's payment check. Free.

tools.name: listing_status
tools.description: Where a watched MCP server stands right now: each directory's status, the latest changes, and when the watch ends. Free.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "builders" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: verify_page, publish_to_registry, check_payment_setup · Private data: enrich_catalog, publish_to_registry, check_payment_setup · Public sink: launch_check, publish_to_registry, watch_listing, launch_plan · Destructive: verify_mcp, publish_to_registry, watch_listing.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: verify_page, publish_to_registry, check_payment_setup · Private data: enrich_catalog, publish_to_registry, check_payment_setup · Public sink: launch_check, publish_to_registry, watch_listing, launch_plan · Destructive: verify_mcp, publish_to_registry, watch_listing

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
